body:
OBJECTIVES
- Students tell a long vowel sound from a short one in spoken one-syllable words (RF.1.2).
- Students know that a final e makes the vowel before it long (RF.1.3).
- Students read and write pairs of words such as cap and cape (RF.1.3).

MATERIALS
- A Magic E wand: a craft stick with a large letter e taped to the top
- Word pair cards: cap/cape, kit/kite, hop/hope, cub/cube, tap/tape, pin/pine
- Two hoops or mats labeled short and long for a sorting game
- Tablets with the class activities open

FIVE-DAY PLAN
Day 1: Read The Magic E together. Tap the Magic E wand on cap to make cape. Students say both words and listen to the vowel.
Day 2: Lesson activity: Watch the Vowel Change. Students read each pair aloud and say whether the vowel is short or long.
Day 3: Make It Magic: students add e to short words and write the new words.
Day 4: Draw the Magic Word: students draw a Magic E word and tell about it. Play the short and long sorting game.
Day 5: Assessment: Short or Long? Read each word aloud twice. Reteach in a small group anyone who still reads cape as cap.

DIFFERENTIATION
- Support: start with a and i only (cap/cape, kit/kite). Let students use the Magic E wand on letter cards.
- Support: accept a spoken answer for Make It Magic and type it together.
- Stretch: find Magic E words in a classroom book and sort them by vowel (a_e, i_e, o_e, u_e).
- Remind all students that Magic E is silent: the e is seen, not heard.

FAMILY NOTE (send home at the start of the unit)
This week we are learning about Magic E, the silent e at the end of words like cake, kite and home. It makes the vowel say its own name. Try writing a short word like hop on paper and let your child add an e to turn it into hope. What other magic words can you make together?
title: Teacher guide: Magic E: Long Vowels
